26 A musical instrument is made using a long tube with a mouthpiece at one end. The other end is
open and flared, as shown.
A musician maintains stationary sound waves with a node at the mouthpiece and an antinode at
the other end. The lowest frequency of sound that the instrument can produce is 92 Hz.
Which different frequencies of sound can be produced by the instrument?
A
92 Hz, 138 Hz, 184 Hz, 230 Hz
B
92 Hz, 184 Hz, 276 Hz, 368 Hz
C
92 Hz, 276 Hz, 460 Hz, 644 Hz
D
92 Hz, 276 Hz, 828 Hz, 1288 Hz

hints: Notice the stated end conditions: a displacement node at the mouthpiece and an antinode at the flared open end.
Recall that a tube closed at one end fits $L = \lambda/4, 3\lambda/4, 5\lambda/4...$ so only odd-numbered harmonics occur.
Multiply the $92\text{ Hz}$ fundamental by $3, 5, 7...$ and check which option list matches $276\text{ Hz}, 460\text{ Hz}, 644\text{ Hz}$.
walkthrough: Identify the pipe type: mouthpiece acts as closed end with a node, flared end is open with an antinode, so it is a closed-open pipe.
For the lowest frequency, the length fits one quarter wavelength: $L = \lambda_1/4$. Higher modes must still fit node to antinode, so $L = n\lambda_n/4$ where $n = 1,3,5,7...$ only.
Since wave speed $v = f\lambda$ is constant, frequency is proportional to $1/\lambda$. So $f_n = n v/(4L) = n f_1$.
With $f_1 = 92\text{ Hz}$, calculate: $3 \times 92 = 276\text{ Hz}$, $5 \times 92 = 460\text{ Hz}$, $7 \times 92 = 644\text{ Hz}$.
Only the list $92\text{ Hz}, 276\text{ Hz}, 460\text{ Hz}, 644\text{ Hz}$ contains odd multiples throughout. This is option C.

A.explanation: Multiples $1, 1.5, 2, 2.5$ times $92\text{ Hz}$ do not satisfy the node-antinode end conditions, which allow only odd-integer multiples.

B.explanation: Multiples $1, 2, 3, 4$ times $92\text{ Hz}$ are all harmonics of a pipe open at both ends, not a pipe closed at one end.

C.explanation: Multiples $1, 3, 5, 7$ times $92\text{ Hz}$ give $92, 276, 460, 644\text{ Hz}$, the odd harmonics of a closed-open pipe.

D.explanation: $1288\text{ Hz}$ is $14 \times 92\text{ Hz}$, an even multiple, so it cannot exist when a node must stay at the mouthpiece and an antinode at the open end.
